PRP Hair Treatment in NYC: How It Works, Sessions and Cost

PRP hair treatment in NYC explained: who it can help, how many sessions you need, how it pairs with a hair transplant, and cost from $395 a session.

2026-09-27

PRP, short for platelet-rich plasma, is one of the most requested non-surgical hair loss treatments in New York. It uses a concentrate made from your own blood to support existing hair follicles. This guide explains what PRP can and cannot do, how many sessions are usually needed, and what it costs at our Midtown Manhattan clinic.

TL;DR
  • PRP uses platelets from your own blood, injected into the scalp to support thinning hair.
  • The American Academy of Dermatology says most patients return once a month for 3 months, then every 3 to 6 months.
  • PRP at Peak NYC starts from $395 per session. It supports existing hair but cannot replace a transplant in fully bald areas.

How PRP works

A small amount of your blood is drawn and spun in a centrifuge to concentrate the platelets. The platelet-rich plasma is then injected into the thinning areas of the scalp. Platelets contain growth factors, and the aim is to support weakened follicles that are still present.

Because PRP works on follicles that still exist, it is generally aimed at thinning hair rather than completely bald areas. Your clinician will assess whether it is suitable for you.

How many PRP sessions will I need?

According to the American Academy of Dermatology, most patients return once a month for 3 months and then once every 3 to 6 months. A review in the medical literature describes a similar schedule: monthly sessions for the first 3 months, then every 3 months for the first year.

PhaseTypical timing
Starting phaseOne session a month for about 3 months
MaintenanceEvery 3 to 6 months, as your clinician advises
ReviewProgress photos compared over several months

Your own schedule depends on your diagnosis and how your hair responds.

Who PRP can help

  • People with early to moderate thinning who still have follicles in the affected areas.
  • Patients who want a non-surgical option or are not ready for a transplant.
  • Hair transplant patients who want to support existing hair around the transplanted area, if their clinician recommends it.

PRP is not a fit for everyone. A clinician will review your medical history, the pattern of your hair loss and any other treatments you use.

PRP vs hair transplant

PRPHair transplant
What it doesSupports existing folliclesMoves follicles from the donor area to thinning areas
Best forThinning hairAreas that have lost follicles
SurgeryNo, injections onlyYes, a minimally invasive procedure
SessionsSeveral, then maintenanceUsually one procedure per area

Some patients use both. Our Sapphire FUE hair transplant page explains the surgical option, and our PRP page explains our PRP treatment in more detail.

PRP hair treatment cost in NYC

PRP at Peak Hair Restoration NYC starts from $395 per session. Because PRP is usually done as a series, ask for the total cost of the starting phase and maintenance during your consultation. Financing through Cherry is available; our NYC cost and financing guide explains how it works.

What to expect on the day

  1. A clinician reviews your scalp, history and goals.
  2. A small blood sample is drawn.
  3. The sample is processed to concentrate the platelets.
  4. The PRP is injected into the treatment areas.
  5. You receive aftercare instructions and plan your next session.

Ask your clinician about any temporary tenderness or swelling to expect, and follow their aftercare instructions.

Frequently asked questions

How much does PRP hair treatment cost in NYC?

At Peak Hair Restoration NYC, PRP starts from $395 per session. Ask for the total cost of your full treatment plan at your consultation.

How many PRP sessions do I need for hair loss?

The American Academy of Dermatology says most patients return once a month for 3 months and then once every 3 to 6 months. Your clinician will set your own schedule.

Can PRP regrow hair on a bald area?

PRP aims to support follicles that are still present, so it is generally used for thinning hair. Areas without follicles may need a hair transplant.

Can I combine PRP with a hair transplant?

Some patients do. Your clinician can advise whether PRP makes sense alongside your transplant plan.
